title: Sex: How to Get More of It: A Guy’s Roadmap to Paradise, In and Out of the Bedroom
author: Robert Mark Alter
target_audience: Men interested in improving their sex lives
Couples wanting to increase intimacy and satisfaction
Adults exploring male perspectives on intimacy
core_themes: Emotional and psychological aspects of sexual relationships
Communication as the foundation of intimacy
Enhancing connection and desire within long-term relationships
Common barriers to sexual satisfaction among men
primary_purpose: To provide men with practical strategies and insights for deepening emotional and physical intimacy with their partners, ultimately leading to a more satisfying and frequent sex life.

structure_format.narrative_style: Direct, humorous, and conversational, with candid stories and anecdotes
structure_format.organization: Divided into topical chapters focused on emotional, relational, and sexual skills
features: Real-life case studies from author’s therapy practice
Myth-busting sections that challenge common male assumptions

key_concepts_lessons: Getting more sex is closely tied to improving non-sexual aspects of the relationship.
Emotional intimacy and honest communication with one's partner foster greater desire and better sex.
Many men underestimate the impact of listening and emotional availability on their sexual relationships.
Common misconceptions about male and female sexuality can hinder sexual satisfaction.
Learning to talk openly about needs, vulnerabilities, and fantasies can transform sex and connection.
Sustained physical attraction is built through daily nurturing, not just sexual advances.
notable_features: Gender-specific focus (advice for men by a male therapist)
Confronts cultural myths about masculinity and sex
cultural_historical_context: Published in the early 2000s during a surge of self-help books for men, this book intersects the emerging 'new masculinity,' encouraging emotional literacy and partnership skills in response to changing expectations of relationships and intimacy.
reception_impact: Appreciated by men seeking realistic, non-gimmicky relationship advice
Praised for combining humor with depth and actionable guidance
Some reviewers note its male-focused approach, though women may also find insights
Seen as refreshingly honest compared to typical 'pickup' or surface-level sex advice books
comparable_titles: She Comes First by Ian Kerner
The Truth: An Uncomfortable Book About Relationships by Neil Strauss
The New Male Sexuality by Bernie Zilbergeld
